stories.headline: US and Iran Exchange Maritime Attacks as Oil Prices Surge Past $100
stories.body:
The United States and Israel launched a military conflict against Iran on February 28, 2026. US President Donald Trump said the war against Iran will end immediately after the upcoming US midterm elections. Trump claimed Iran is stalling an end to the war. He said Iran wants to secure a more favorable political environment in the US ahead of the midterms.

A poll conducted in August 2026 showed that only 31 percent of Americans support the war in Iran. Support was down from 37 percent in March 2026. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright spoke about future actions. Wright said the US may continue strikes against Iranian nuclear infrastructure instead of reaching a nuclear deal.

Trump said that the US military has knocked out about nine Iranian oil tankers. US Central Command gave more details on these actions. Central Command said its strikes destroyed four Iranian tankers in the Gulf of Oman. These four ships were named Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1, and Riesco. Central Command said a fifth Iranian tanker named Derya was destroyed near Kharg Island.

Iran said that it attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran said it launched these attacks after the US military sank five Iranian oil tankers. An attack occurred on an oil products tanker named Hercules Star off Dubai. One seafarer was killed aboard the ship. Another seafarer was reported missing after the attack.

The Iranian Revolutionary Guards made a warning against further attacks. They said that they would hit 20 targets if their enemy struck two or three targets. Revolutionary Guard spokesman Hossein Mohebi announced plans to mark a new prohibited zone. Mohebi said Iran will set coordinates for this zone. The new prohibited zone will cover parts of the Sea of Oman and the Arabian Sea.

Jordan's armed forces reported intercepting 20 Iranian missiles. These missiles were aimed at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base. Jordan reported no casualties from the missile interception.

Energy markets saw sharp price rises during the military actions. Benchmark Brent crude futures breached $100 a barrel. This was the first time Brent crude passed $100 since July 2026. The Dutch benchmark gas contract rose by almost 4% to €78.73 a megawatt hour. This reached its highest level since January 2023. China's crude oil imports recovered to nearly 9 million barrels per day in August 2026. That figure was up from 7.15 million barrels per day in June.

claims.text: The military conflict against Iran was launched on February 28, 2026, by the US and Israel.
US President Donald Trump stated that the war against Iran will end immediately after the upcoming US midterm elections.
US President Donald Trump claimed Iran is stalling an end to the war to secure a more favorable political environment in the US ahead of the midterms.
A poll conducted in August 2026 showed that only 31 percent of Americans support the war in Iran, down from 37 percent in March.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated that the US may continue strikes against Iranian nuclear infrastructure instead of reaching a nuclear deal.
US President Donald Trump stated that the US military has knocked out about nine Iranian oil tankers.
US Central Command stated its strikes destroyed four Iranian tankers in the Gulf of Oman—Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1, and Riesco—and a fifth tanker, Derya, near Kharg Island.
Iran stated it attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the US military sank five Iranian oil tankers.
One seafarer was killed and another was reported missing aboard the oil products tanker Hercules Star off Dubai following an attack.
The Iranian Revolutionary Guards stated they would hit 20 targets if their enemy struck two or three targets.
IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebi announced plans to set coordinates for a new prohibited zone covering parts of the Sea of Oman and the Arabian Sea.
Jordan's armed forces reported intercepting 20 Iranian missiles aimed at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, with no casualties reported.
Benchmark Brent crude futures breached $100 a barrel for the first time since July 2026.
The Dutch benchmark gas contract rose by almost 4% to €78.73 a megawatt hour, reaching its highest level since January 2023.
China's crude oil imports recovered to nearly 9 million barrels per day in August 2026, up from 7.15 million in June.

stories.headline: Apple Unveils Foldable iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro Series
stories.body:
Apple unveiled its first foldable smartphone named the iPhone Duo at a starting price of $1,999. The device opens into a horizontal 7.6-inch-wide screen. Apple made the iPhone Duo an eSIM-only device globally by completely removing the physical SIM tray. The iPhone Duo omits Face ID and uses a Touch ID sensor in the power button. Apple claims the phone offers up to 31 hours of video playback on its inner display. It offers up to 44 hours on its outer display.

In India, the iPhone Duo starts at Rs 2,99,900 for the 256GB model. The 2TB model costs up to Rs 4,49,900. Apple also raised the base price of the standard iPhone 17 in India to Rs 99,900. It increased the ultra-thin iPhone Air price by Rs 30,000 to Rs 1,49,900.

Apple announced pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max begin on September 12, 2026. Stores will have them on September 18, 2026. The 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900 in India. The 18 Pro Max starts at Rs 1,79,900. The 18 Pro series runs on an A20 Pro 2-nanometer processor. It includes Apple Reference Image to verify photo authenticity.

Apple also introduced the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4. Both watches run on the new S11 processor. They feature native daily tracking called Readiness score.

claims.text: Apple unveiled its first foldable smartphone, named the iPhone Duo, starting at a price of $1,999.
The iPhone Duo opens into a horizontal 7.6-inch-wide screen.
Apple made the iPhone Duo an eSIM-only device globally by completely eliminating the physical SIM tray.
The iPhone Duo omits Face ID in favor of a Touch ID sensor embedded in the power button to save internal space.
Apple claims the iPhone Duo delivers up to 31 hours of video playback on its inner display and up to 44 hours on its outer display.
In India, the iPhone Duo starts at Rs 2,99,900 for the 256GB model and ranges up to Rs 4,49,900 for the 2TB model.
Apple raised the base price of the standard iPhone 17 in India from Rs 82,900 to Rs 99,900.
Apple increased the retail price of the ultra-thin iPhone Air in India by Rs 30,000, bringing it to Rs 1,49,900.
Apple announced that pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max begin on September 12, 2026, with store availability starting September 18, 2026.
In India, the iPhone 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at Rs 1,79,900.
The iPhone 18 Pro series is powered by Apple's A20 Pro processor built on 2-nanometer technology.
The iPhone 18 Pro lineup introduces Apple Reference Image, a feature that uses signed sensor data to verify photo authenticity.
Apple introduced the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, both equipped with the new S11 processor.
Apple introduced native 'Readiness score' daily tracking across its new smartwatches.

stories.headline: IAEA Board Reports Iran to UN Security Council Over Nuclear Obligations
stories.body:
The International Atomic Energy Agency Board of Governors reported Iran to the UN Security Council for nuclear non-compliance. This resolution marks the first time in 20 years that the 35-member board has reported Iran. The United Kingdom, France, Germany, and the United States submitted the resolution together. Twenty-three countries voted in favor of the measure. Russia, China, and Niger voted against it.

The IAEA suspects Iran holds about 400 kilograms of highly enriched uranium. That amount could produce 10 nuclear weapons if enriched further. Senior US officials said Iran had about 440 kilograms of 60% enriched uranium when the latest conflict started.

Iran's mission to the UN said the non-compliance was caused entirely by aggression from the US and Israel. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said US and Israeli attacks disrupted nuclear inspections. He said those attacks were then used as a pretext for the resolution. Iran circulated an 11-page document warning Western nations not to turn the IAEA into a tool of war. China, Russia, and Iran said the vote risks politicizing a technical matter. US President Donald Trump said the US may soon hit the Pickaxe facility south of Natanz.

claims.text: The IAEA Board of Governors passed a resolution reporting Iran to the UN Security Council for non-compliance with its non-proliferation obligations.
Wednesday's resolution by the 35-member IAEA board is the first time in 20 years that Iran has been reported to the UN Security Council.
The IAEA resolution against Iran was submitted jointly by the United Kingdom, France, Germany, and the United States.
Twenty-three countries voted in favor of the IAEA resolution reporting Iran, while Russia, China, and Niger voted against it.
The IAEA suspects Iran holds approximately 400kg of highly enriched uranium, sufficient to potentially produce 10 nuclear weapons if further enriched.
Senior US officials stated that Iran possessed roughly 440kg of 60% enriched uranium at the start of the latest conflict.
Iran's mission to the UN stated that the nuclear non-compliance situation was created solely because of criminal acts of aggression by the US and Israel.
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated that US and Israeli attacks disrupted nuclear inspections and were then used as a pretext to pass an IAEA resolution.
Iran circulated an 11-page diplomatic document warning Western nations against converting the IAEA into a tool of war.
China, Russia, and Iran rejected the legal basis of the IAEA vote, arguing that reporting Iran risks politicizing a technical matter.
US President Donald Trump stated on September 4 that the US may soon hit the Pickaxe facility south of Natanz.

stories.headline: Twelve Nations Impose Trade Sanctions on West Bank Israeli Settlements
stories.body:
Twelve countries coordinated new sanctions targeting trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The coalition includes Britain, France, and Canada. UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced the British trade sanctions on the settlements. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham defended the new trade ban. Last year, exports from occupied territories to the UK totaled $45 million out of $4.4 billion in total trade.

UK Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis condemned the sanctions as a dark day for British Jews. But prominent British rabbis Jonathan Wittenberg and Alexandra Wright publicly supported the sanctions. Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert and former military chief Dan Halutz signed a statement welcoming the UK measures. A poll showed nearly three-quarters of Jewish Israelis support partial or total annexation of the West Bank.

Miliband said Israeli intelligence promised that intelligence sharing with the UK will continue unchanged. US President Donald Trump said he will speak to Israel about the sanctions. The UK government also announced fresh nuclear-related sanctions against Iranian ships.

claims.text: Twelve countries, including Britain, France, and Canada, coordinated to sanction trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced sweeping UK sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham defended a trade ban on products from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
Exports from occupied territories to the UK totaled $45 million last year out of $4.4 billion in total trade between the UK and Israel.
UK Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis condemned the UK settlement sanctions, describing the decision as a 'dark day for British Jews'.
Prominent British rabbis, including Masorti Rabbi Jonathan Wittenberg and Liberal Rabbi Alexandra Wright, publicly voiced support for the UK settlement sanctions.
Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert and former military chief Dan Halutz signed a joint statement welcoming the UK sanctions on settlements.
A poll by the Jewish People Policy Institute found that nearly three-quarters of Jewish Israelis support partial or total annexation of the occupied West Bank.
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband stated that Israeli intelligence gave assurances that intelligence sharing with the UK will continue unchanged despite the trade sanctions.
US President Donald Trump stated he would speak to Israel to find out their thinking regarding the settlement sanctions imposed by allied nations.
The UK government announced fresh nuclear-related sanctions targeting Iranian ships involved in malign behavior.

stories.headline: Republicans Open Midterm Convention in Dallas With Trump as Speaker
stories.body:
Republican National Committee Chair Joe Gruters opened the party's two-day midterm convention in Dallas, Texas. The gathering at the American Airlines Center is the first midterm convention held by the Republican Party. US President Donald Trump is set as the main speaker for both nights. Before Trump left for Dallas, an emergency inflatable slide on Air Force One deployed by accident.

The pro-Trump Super PAC Maga Inc holds a $400 million fund. It set aside $47 million for seven competitive midterm races. The convention schedule contains 109 items, including a segment on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks. It leaves out any segment on the ongoing war with Iran.

A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed Trump with an approval rating of 33 percent. Another poll by FT/Focaldata found that 57 percent of respondents feel their personal finances got worse after Trump took office. In Missouri, legal challengers filed an emergency appeal with the US Supreme Court. They are fighting a federal judge's order that forces Missouri to use a new Republican-drawn map in the midterms.

claims.text: Republican National Committee Chair Joe Gruters opened the two-day Republican midterm convention at the American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas.
The gathering at the American Airlines Center in Dallas is the first midterm convention held by the Republican Party.
Republicans organized the midterm convention in Dallas with US President Donald Trump slated as the primary keynote speaker for both nights.
An emergency inflatable slide on Air Force One was accidentally deployed prior to Donald Trump's departure to Dallas.
The pro-Trump Super PAC Maga Inc holds a $400 million war chest and earmarked $47 million for seven competitive midterm races.
The 109-item schedule for the Republican convention includes a segment on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks but excludes any segment on the ongoing war with Iran.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed US President Donald Trump with an approval rating of 33 percent.
An FT/Focaldata poll indicated that 57 percent of respondents believe their personal financial situation has worsened since Donald Trump re-took office.
Challengers of Missouri's congressional redistricting map filed an emergency appeal with the US Supreme Court after a federal judge ordered Missouri to use a new Republican-drawn map in the midterms.

stories.headline: German Chancellor Merz Cancels Trump Call After Far-Right Election Victory
stories.body:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz cancelled a planned phone call with US President Donald Trump. Merz took the action after Trump praised a far-right election victory in Germany. Trump posted on Truth Social to celebrate the win by the Alternative für Deutschland party, ending his message with MGGA.

The AfD won 43.8% of the vote in the Saxony-Anhalt state election on September 6. The result left the AfD three seats short of an absolute majority. The Christian Democratic Union saw its vote share fall to 17.2%, down from 37.1% in 2021. Voter turnout reached nearly 78%.

In a parliament debate, Merz accused the AfD of seeking ethnic cleansing. He said one in six skilled workers in Germany has a migration background. Merz also criticized the AfD for not condemning a drone attack at Leipzig airport linked to Russia. AfD co-leader Alice Weidel said Merz's coalition had failed and his time as chancellor was up. Bundestag President Julia Klöckner threatened to expel shouting AfD lawmakers. In Serbia, President Aleksandar Vučić dissolved parliament for snap elections in October 2026.

claims.text: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz cancelled a planned telephone call with US President Donald Trump after Trump publicly praised the AfD's state election victory.
US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social celebrating the AfD's election victory and ended his statement with 'MGGA!!!'.
The far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) won 43.8% of the vote in the Saxony-Anhalt state election on September 6.
The AfD won nearly 44% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt but fell three seats short of an absolute majority.
The Christian Democratic Union (CDU) vote share in Saxony-Anhalt fell to 17.2%, down from 37.1% in 2021.
Voter turnout in the Saxony-Anhalt state election reached nearly 78%.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz accused the AfD of seeking 'ethnic cleansing' during a Bundestag parliamentary debate.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated in parliament that one in six skilled workers in Germany has a migration background.

AfD co-leader Alice Weidel told the Bundestag that Friedrich Merz's coalition was a failure and that his time as chancellor was up.
Bundestag President Julia Klöckner threatened to expel shouting AfD lawmakers from the chamber during the parliamentary debate.
Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić dissolved parliament and announced snap elections for October 2026.

stories.headline: Delhi Inspects PG Hostels After Fatal Satya Niketan Building Collapse
stories.body:
Seven people died when a five-storey building collapsed in Delhi's Satya Niketan area on September 6. Work done 10 days before the collapse put about three truckloads of debris into the basement. On the day of the collapse, workers removed a ground-floor wall to expand a shop. Police arrested labor contractor Sanoj Kumar for supervising the renovation. Police also arrested PG operator Sudhanshu, while his associate Shubham Tyagi remained on the run. Property owners Hariram Bansal and Urmila Gupta were sent to 14 days of judicial custody.

Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered the demolition of an adjoining dilapidated building. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi then inspected 1,252 paying guest accommodation buildings. Officials found 1,201 safe, 39 needing minor repairs, nine needing major repairs, and three dangerous. The agency also picked 26 tall structures above four upper floors for close monitoring.

Student activists reported mobile internet slowdowns in the area and claimed jammers were used. Delhi Police denied the claim and said networks were operational. Meanwhile, India's Supreme Court agreed to review compliance rules for illegal PG structures across the country.

claims.text: Seven people were killed when the five-storey building in Satya Niketan collapsed on September 6.
Renovation work conducted around 10 days before the collapse involved filling approximately three truckloads of construction debris into the basement of the Satya Niketan building.
On the day of the collapse, a wall on the ground floor of the Satya Niketan building was removed to create additional space for a shop.
Police apprehended and arrested 35-year-old labour contractor Sanoj Kumar from Kasganj in Uttar Pradesh for supervising the renovation work.
Delhi Police arrested Sudhanshu, operator of the 'Hostel Daze' PG facility housed inside the collapsed Satya Niketan building, while co-operator Shubham Tyagi remained on the run.
Property owners Hariram Bansal, aged 81, and Urmila Gupta, aged 75, were sent to 14 days of judicial custody following the building collapse.
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered the Municipal Corporation of Delhi to demolish the dilapidated building adjoining the collapse site.
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi surveyed 1,252 paying guest accommodation buildings between September 7 and 9 following the Satya Niketan building collapse.
Out of 1,252 surveyed PG buildings, 1,201 were found visibly safe, 39 required minor repairs, 9 required major repairs, and 3 were declared dangerous.
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi identified 26 framed structures above G+4 floors for close monitoring due to structural vulnerability.
Following the building collapse, local journalists and student activists reported severe mobile internet slowdowns in Satya Niketan and alleged the government had used jammers.
Delhi Police issued a social media statement denying internet slowdown allegations, stating that networks were fully operational in Satya Niketan.
A Supreme Court bench comprising Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R Mahadevan agreed to examine regulatory compliance regarding illegal PG structures on a pan-India basis.

stories.headline: India Prepares to Host 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi
stories.body:
India is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit on September 12 and 13, 2026, in New Delhi. The event takes place at Bharat Mandapam. The official theme for the summit is Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will host a gala dinner for participating leaders on Saturday evening.

Modi has planned key two-way talks with international leaders during the summit. He is scheduled to hold a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday. On Saturday, Modi is scheduled to hold a formal meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Economic discussions between India and Russia are also taking place alongside the summit preparations. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal will meet Russian counterpart Anton Alikhanov on Thursday. Their meeting takes place at the INNOPROM India 2026 industrial trade fair. The trade fair runs at Bharat Mandapam from September 9 to 11. India and Russia have set a target to reach $100 billion in bilateral trade by 2030. That amount equals approximately Rs 9.45 lakh crore.

India is also developing its internal trade networks. The National Industrial Corridor Development Programme covers 11 industrial corridors. It includes 20 greenfield industrial smart cities spread across 13 Indian states.

The BRICS group has grown significantly since its founding. It started as the BRIC alliance between Brazil, Russia, India, and China in 2006. The group held its first summit in Yekaterinburg in 2009. South Africa joined the group in 2011. BRICS expanded to 11 full member states in recent years. It admitted Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates in January 2024. Indonesia joined as a full member in January 2025.

Authorities in New Delhi have put detailed security and traffic measures in place for the summit. Delhi Traffic Police set up 22 diversion points across the city. They are regulating traffic on more than 35 roads. Roadside parking within 200 meters of controlled roads is strictly forbidden. But Delhi Metro operations will run normally without any disruption across all stations.

Air travel infrastructure has also been expanded for summit guests. Delhi International Airport Limited opened Pier C at Terminal 3 on the night of September 9. The airport created dedicated immigration counters for summit participants. It also made special arrangements for airplane landing and parking.

The National Industrial Corridor Development Programme spans 11 industrial corridors and 20 greenfield industrial smart cities across 13 Indian states.
BRICS originated as the BRIC alliance between Brazil, Russia, India, and China in 2006, held its first summit in Yekaterinburg in 2009, and admitted South Africa in 2011.
BRICS expanded to 11 full member states after admitting Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE in January 2024, followed by Indonesia in January 2025.
Delhi Traffic Police issued a public advisory establishing 22 diversion points and regulating traffic across more than 35 roads for the BRICS summit.
Roadside parking within 200 metres of controlled roads during the BRICS summit period is strictly prohibited in Delhi.
